by: Behaviour Designer, team Not A Screensaver (Design round: Last Five; Build round: the seat after, Nov 11 2026)
what: How Potato behaves, written as data. A small engine of ours reads this file (and direction.json for the feel numbers) and runs him locally with no live brain. Nothing in here knows about a desktop: the host (desktop pet, game, door page) turns its own inputs into the events listed under inputs, and that is the only join. Plain-words manual: design/BEHAVIOUR.md.

units.time: seconds unless the key ends in _ms
units.ranges: [min, max]: the engine draws a fresh value every time from the seeded generator; a single number is exact
units.distance: body_widths or body heights of this Potato unless the key ends in _px (screen pixels, desktop only: the host converts)

witness.note: The director's flag. When false, needs.watched is treated as always true and behaviours tagged private never run.

overnight.note: BOLD CHOICE (Last Five, Design round): he remembers how you left it. OFF TONIGHT by the director's ruling (it needs the pet to save between launches). Not killed. See overnight below.

door_spot.note: BOLD CHOICE (Potato seat): WHERE THE DOOR WAS. Mirror of data/potato-calls.json flags.door_spot. After a trip into the 404 his home spot moves to the floor under where the hole was, for the session. Nothing is drawn. The brain sets it when a first contact of kind 'hole' is claimed by a move; until a 404 move exists it never fires.

unfinished_business.note: BOLD CHOICE (Behaviour Designer, Build round): what you interrupt is not dropped. A body behaviour cut short before its last beat, or a burst he was owed in an argument you broke up, is remembered (two at most) and comes back once, 40 to 120 s later, from the beat he was on. false = an interrupted behaviour is simply gone, as before.

stance.note: Round 3 (director B1: mood must show in how he stands). When the mood on top changes and he is alone, one slow turn to that mood's stance yaw; 'home' in every later turn means that yaw until the mood changes again. Unbothered is yaw 0: the canon rest pose is untouched. In a crowd his angle is his place in the clump instead (crowd.clumps.facing). Lower-and-wider for low power can only be played once as he enters it: a HELD squash is the animator's carriage (she stores the moods and does not use them yet). false = no stance turns.

closing_ranks.note: BOLD CHOICE (Behaviour Designer, round 3): CLOSING RANKS. You throw one of them. When he is back on his feet and has given you his look, the two nearest walk over, stand either side of him, and all three turn their backs on you and hold it. Nobody looks at you. Then they drift apart one at a time. Needs three or more; at most every at_most_every_s. false = off (the others only follow the throw with their bodies, as before).

determinism.rule: The behaviour layer is a pure function of (this file, direction.json, seed, the timed list of input events, the overnight state passed in). Same four things in, same timeline out, on any machine.
determinism.generator: mulberry32. One stream per Potato: seed XOR a 32-bit hash of the Potato's id. Every draw (which behaviour, every range, every side flip, every variant) comes from that stream in a fixed order. No Math.random, no wall clock, no frame count: time is the fixed 60 Hz step count.
determinism.seed_sources: bench.html?seed=1234 for strips; the pet uses the launch time as its seed and writes it in the trace header so any moment can be replayed.
determinism.fast_run: The picker must run without rendering: simulate(seconds, seed, events) returns the timeline (time, potato, behaviour or reaction id, dominant mood, mood weights). tools/behaviour_check.py is a reference copy of the pick rule in Python that does this today and counts repeats.

repeat_test.measured_design_round: Nov 11, tools/behaviour_check.py, idles only (reactions stood in for by their mood pushes), 20 seeds x 3 scenarios (watched, bothered, alone) = 60 runs. 10 min: 0 back-to-back, 0 repeated triples, worst share 7.7%, 23 to 36 distinct behaviours a run, 74 to 84% of picks on-mood; time at home averages 56% watched, 38% bothered, 64% alone (single runs range from 19% to 89%). 60 min: 0 and 0 again, 37 to 47 distinct, worst share 6.9%. min_distinct started at 25 and was moved to 22 after measuring (worst run 23): said here so nobody thinks it always passed. Not measured: anything with reactions, a crowd, or a personality.
repeat_test.pass_if_note: Pass marks re-measured in the Build round IN THE ENGINE (engine/behaviour/tools/life.mjs: the real brain.mjs on a paper body, and tools in strips/behaviour for the bench run). With the slower pace a ten-minute life has far fewer picks, so min_distinct_behaviours was re-set from the measurement and the old 22 no longer applies. Set Nov 11 from measured_build_round: worst run did 20 different things (mark = that minus 2) and matched its mood on 69% of picks (mark 65%; the Design-round mark was 70% on 50 picks a run, a run now has about 40).

moods.note: He is always in a BLEND. Each mood has a pressure (0 or more). weight = pressure^sharpen / sum of all pressure^sharpen. The weights feed direction.json moods.list (every feel number is the weighted mix) and the picker (affinity). Pressures ease back to rest with their own half-life, events push them, and now and then a whim pushes one for no reason.

dominant.rule: The dominant mood is the highest weight. It only changes when another weight beats it by switch_margin, and then holds at least min_hold_s, so he does not flicker between moods.

readable.rule: He must always be recognisably in a mood. Three guards: (1) the carriage of the dominant mood is always on (posture, lids, base face, how long he waits), so the mood reads even when nothing is playing; (2) at least 70% of picks in any minute have affinity 0.5 or more for the dominant mood; (3) if the top weight falls under floor, the engine raises sharpen for that step until it does not.

whim.note: The drift under everything: with no input at all he still changes mood. Every every_s a whim pushes one non-home mood. Smug and rattled are never a whim: each needs a cause (Potato seat).

unbothered.see: Side-eye, long holds, slow breath. Home.

stance.see: Square on, his side-eye home. The canon rest pose.

nosy.see: Eyes on the cursor or the other Potato, a lean toward it, drifting to the edges.

stance.see: Turned a little toward the thing, and a lean at it as he gets there.

smug.see: A hint of smirk, slow blinks, a touch taller.

stance.see: Square on and a touch taller.

fed_up.see: Angled away from you, lids lower, stiff.

stance.see: Turned three-quarters away from you, and stays there.

rattled.see: Eyes wider, breath quick and shallow, never quite still.

stance.see: Snaps square: nothing behind him he has not checked.

low_power.see: Drooping, long blinks. Deep Rest, never death.

stance.see: Sags: lower and wider, and holds it.

settles_into.note: Where a mood's pressure goes as it eases off, instead of just vanishing. share = part of the lost pressure handed on.

pushes.note: What moves him between moods. Each reaction rung carries its own push; these are the pushes that belong to no single rung. per_s entries apply every second while true.

pace.note: Two clocks (director's ruling 11, the Potato seat's pace). gap_s = the EYES: a micro behaviour may start this long after the last thing ended. body_gap_s = the BODY: a small or big behaviour may start this long after the last BODY thing ended. Unbothered he does a body thing every 20 to 45 s and now and then goes quiet_stretch_s with only breath, blink and eyes.
pace.cap_note: Round 3 (director B1): no gap between body behaviours over 45 s. The body clock is drawn as before, but cap_lead_s before the cap (drawn fresh each time, so the cap is never a metronome) he MUST do a body thing: the picker relaxes mood quota, share cap, travel gap, then cooldowns (halved). It never relaxes the no-repeat rules. A quiet stretch is now 32 to 42 s (was 60 to 120): the two long gaps the director measured (128, 121 s) were quiet stretches.

smug_cause.what_counts: any reaction rung, argument result or refusal that pushed smug above 0
smug_cause.rule: Idles with needs.smug_cause_within_s only run inside that window. A smirk for no reason is a mascot smiling.

drives.note: Two slow needs under the moods. Both 0..1.

boredom.falls_on: any direct input (-0.5), finishing a big behaviour (-0.4), a crowd bit (-0.3)
boredom.effect: over 0.5: behaviours tagged travel, inspect, edge and prop get weight x(1 + boredom). It is why he eventually does something for himself.

energy.effect: under 0.3 it feeds low_power every second (moods.pushes.energy_low). Fries are food: tokens are metabolism. At 0 he sleeps; he never dies.

watch.note: THE WITNESS RULE, as states. Numbers come from direction.json watched.

states.watched: The cursor has moved in the last gone_after_s. Every gag may end in a check (a look at the cursor) and a cover-up. needs.watched:true behaviours can run.
states.unwatched: The cursor has been still for gone_after_s. cursor_gone fires once. needs.watched:false (tag private) behaviours can run; nothing ends in a check; no cover-ups.
states.returning: The first cursor movement after unwatched. cursor_returned fires; whatever was running ends through its cover exit; then watched.

watch.in_the_game: The game has no cursor. Its host decides what 'watched' means (the camera is on him and the player has pressed something lately) and sends the same two events.

tiers.micro: Eyes and face only. May play over a hold or over the carriage. Never blocks the body.
tiers.small: A body behaviour. One at a time per Potato.
tiers.big: A set piece. One at a time per Potato, at least direction.json tempo.min_gap_between_big_bits_s since his last one, and in a crowd it needs the stage (crowd.stage). After it: hold tempo.hold_after_big_bit_ms.

picker.note: How the next idle is chosen. This is the whole what-leads-to-what rule; the per-behaviour 'then' lists are its weighted edges.
picker.when: When his body is free (no reaction, no physics owning him), wait one gap drawn from the dominant mood's gap_s (he holds: carriage, breath, blinks, eye drift), then pick.
eligible: not on its own cooldown (cooldown_s, scaled per Potato by a fixed draw of 0.8..1.25 so two Potatoes do not share a rhythm)
not among the last history.no_repeat_last picks
the pair (previous, this) has not happened in the last history.no_repeat_pair_within transitions
the triple (two before, previous, this) has not happened in the last history.no_repeat_triple_within transitions
tier rules pass (big gap, crowd stage)
tagged travel: none in the last travel_min_gap_s
needs.smug_cause_within_s: a smug cause inside that many seconds
picker.score: w x affinity x novelty x follow x drive x personality

terms.affinity: (sum over moods of mood weight x this behaviour's moods value), squared, so the blend leans hard on the moods he is most in. Not listed = 0.
terms.private_ramp: behaviours tagged private are also multiplied by the private ramp (see private).
terms.novelty: never played: 1. Otherwise min(1, time_since_last / (3 x cooldown_s)): things come back slowly after their cooldown ends.
terms.follow: 1 + 2 x w if the previous behaviour's 'then' lists this one, else 1. A 'then' entry with chain:true means: straight after, with probability w and no gap, if its needs and cooldown allow. A chain is ONE sentence: for the history rules only its first behaviour counts.
terms.drive: boredom and ignored-ladder boosts by tag, and x3 for behaviours a current ignored rung lists under prefer.
terms.personality: product of the personality's tag multipliers for this behaviour's tags (personalities.dials).

picker.choose: Weighted random over eligible scores from the Potato's seeded stream. If nothing is eligible he simply holds for another gap (a hold is the default state, not a behaviour, so it can never count as a repeat).

mood_quota.rule: Of his last over_last picks, at most off_mood_at_most may have affinity under 0.5 for the mood that was dominant when they were picked. Once that many are off-mood, only on-mood behaviours are eligible. This is the guard that keeps him recognisably in a mood.

variation_inside_a_behaviour: sideA / sideB are assigned left or right by a coin flip per play (biased 60/40 away from the side used last time)
every hold is scaled by the dominant mood's gap midpoint relative to home
pick:a,b,c values draw one, never the one drawn last time
the feel numbers under every move (anticipation, overshoot, stiffness, breath) come from the mood blend in direction.json, so the same beats land differently in a different mood
picker.share_cap: No behaviour may be more than 8% of picks over any 10 minutes (counted against at least 25 picks, so the cap does not bite in the first minutes); over the cap it is not eligible until it is back under.

own_glitch.paced_by: Chikin, Nov 12 2026 night: "his model doesnt glitch on its own, hes supposed to glitch, it can be more subtle when hes just chilling or strolling". Was every 170 to 225 s, first at 60 to 140 s (round 3). The measured own_glitches counts in this file are from the old pace.
own_glitch.note: Round 3 (director B1: he is a glitch character; one small purple flicker of his own at least every 3 to 4 minutes). When due, the picker is asked for a behaviour tagged self_glitch (glitch_flicker, aftershock_twitch, hiccup_glitch; try_the_glitch when you are gone). The animator claims the glitch channel and has no glitch verb, so until she gives one an idle glitch beat plays carrier_move (her own stepped purple twitch). A zap resets the clock. off: on = false.

verbs.note: What a beat can say. A beat is one object; every verb in it starts together; 't' is how long the beat lasts. Beats run in order. The engine maps verbs onto createSpud's api, the live face, the parent group and spudphys. Verbs marked (animator) or (engineer) name a move those seats own; this file only says when.
verbs.look: Eyes only. Targets: cursor, cursor_rest (where it last stopped), away (opposite the cursor), home (canon side-eye), front, up, down, sideA, sideB, behind, nothing (a seeded empty spot), edge, spot (where he just stood), home_spot (where he lives), interest (cursor or nearest Potato, whichever moved last), other, stage (whoever holds the stage), self_a/self_b/self_c (points on his own body), crack, hole, prop, heading, text, text_caret. Options beside it: track (keep following), speed (slow/fast), stepped. His eyes have a home side (the animator: pupils sit in the screen-right corner), so a look his eyes cannot reach becomes eyes as far as they go plus a small turn: the engine decides, the beat does not change. Build round: other also means the focus of a crowd bit; away_from_other; thing (what a refusal is about).
verbs.blink: normal, slow, double, hold_closed (stay shut until the next blink or a sleep:false). The background blink process (direction.json eyes) keeps running under everything except hold_closed. (animator)
verbs.face: {to, k}: take his face toward one of the 26 expression faces; k is how far. skeptical at k 1 = home. 'pick:a,b' draws one. HOW it changes is the animator's rule (moves.json blend): lids and brows move live, and the drawn face itself changes on one frame under a blink or inside an impact, never as a cross-fade.
verbs.turn: {to, speed, amount, eyes, by}: yaw. to: cursor, away, home, front, back, behind, sideA, sideB, other, edge, away_from_edge, spot, text. by = radians for spins. eyes: stay_then_follow / stay_on_cursor. Build round: away_from_other (side-on, facing away from him).
verbs.lean: {x|z|toward, amount, grow, past_edge}: held lean on the parent group (the model eats lean set on itself: board trap 1). amount 0 = release.
verbs.squash: {to, hold}: held squash (under 1) or stretch (over 1) on the parent group, volume kept. hold:false releases to 1.
verbs.kick: {spring, v}: an impulse on one of his own springs (squash, wob, leanX, leanZ).
verbs.walk: {to, body_widths, stop_short_px, speed, speed_scale, facing, from, wander}: waddle. to: as look targets plus far_from_cursor, away_from_crack, offscreen edges. facing: keep (does not turn to walk: a shuffle) / away. Build round: to other with stop_short_bw; away_from_other; past_other; free_spot (the nearest spot nobody is standing on).
verbs.hop: {h}: a hop of h body heights through our physics (never the model's own hop(): board trap 3).
verbs.arms: none, up (existing ARM_POSES). Only where he needs them: balance. The fries need none: he leans in face first (the comedian). No hands, ever.
verbs.glitch: {k, kind, steps, fade}: purple, on him, stepped at 12 fps. kind is the personality's own for script Potatoes.
verbs.prop: {id, on}: fries, smoke_wisp. Ink only, no white lines.
verbs.cue: true: the one place in this behaviour where its sound cue may land (see sound_contract). This file never names a sound; data/sounds.json decides. Body sounds (plop, skid, zap, crack) are fired by physics.
verbs.breath: {depth_scale, period_scale}: bends the breath for this beat.
verbs.sleep: true / false: asleep flag (lids shut, events 'asleep' true).
verbs.move: A named move from data/moves.json (the animator's): gather, settle, sigh, chew, one_nub, get_up, bite_cursor, bump, hang, set_down, down, late_twitch, caught_looking, lean_on_edge. Ones not there yet are listed in moves_wanted. Options beside it: stiff, rate_hz, repeat, target, until. Build round: a behaviour or variant may carry whole_move (the animator's one move IS the bit: fries), and a reaction first_move (her clip first, then the acting written here: zap, squish_flat, explode). Used only when her moves.mjs has that move.
verbs.hold: Hold the result. Never frozen: carriage, breath, blinks and eye drift go on. flat:true = stay flattened.
verbs.resume: Go back to the behaviour that was interrupted, from the beat it was on.
verbs.emit: Send a named event to the host or the crowd (hole_shut, eyes_in_hole).
verbs.shove: {level: bump | shove | big_shove}: the contact frame of a push on 'other', through crowd.shove: the same physics as the user's throw. Withheld (and logged shove_withheld) unless the other is up, awake and on the ground: REAL, NOT MEAN.
verbs.lunge: {toward, body_widths} / {amount: 0}: a short drive of his body toward something and back, on top of where he stands (he does not walk).
verbs.bob: {n, amount}: n short body bobs. The argue burst.

interrupts.note: What may cut a behaviour short, and how it leaves.
interrupts.always: Physical events (poked, picked_up, dragged, thrown, zapped, squished, splatted, exploded, a hit from another Potato) interrupt everything, at once, through the blend layer. Nothing is immune.

yields_to.social: other_near, crowd bids and audience duty

exit.blend: blend out from wherever it is, within judge.max_blend_jump per frame
exit.finish_beat: finish the current beat (at most 0.4 s more) then blend out
exit.cover: the cursor_returned cover-up plays as its exit: snap back, hold too still
exit.wake: leaves through sleep:false and a wake variant

inputs.note: The only place a host touches this file: it turns what it has into these events. Thresholds here are STARTING values for the engineer to correct. The game sends the same events from its own world (an enemy's hit = poked, a launcher = thrown).

poked.desktop: press and release on him within click_max_ms, moving less than move_max_px

picked_up.desktop: press held past hold_min_ms or moved past move_max_px

thrown.desktop: released faster than throw_min (body heights per second)
thrown.note: by = user or a Potato id: one Potato throwing another sends this same event. Crack and hole are NOT release speeds: they are the speed into the surface at first contact, in data/physics.json (and they learn the user's hand).

landed.from: physics, every rest after being airborne

cracked.from: the engine's contact event with first: true and kind: 'crack' (there is no separate event)

went_through.from: the engine's contact event with first: true and kind: 'hole'

ignored.from: engine clock: quiet_s since the last direct input

cursor_near.desktop: pointer distance and speed, every step

window_edge.from: engine: his walk reached a screen edge

typed_at.desktop: keys in HIS text box only

zapped.desktop: the host's zap control (engineer's call what it is)

squished.desktop: the host's squish control, or pressed flat against an edge by a drag

splatted.from: the engine's contact event with first: true and kind: 'splat'

shoved.from: crowd: another Potato's shove landed on him

said.from: the thinking one's line (the real brain later; tonight crowd.thinking_one.lines)

refusal.note: THE NO (the Comedian's bold choice; flag and numbers live in design/gags.json refusals / refusal). When a reaction or behaviour that names a gag is about to start, the engine rolls the refusal first. A NO is three fixed beats (eyes to the thing, eyes to you and hold, turn away). For this file a NO counts as a variant: it obeys never-twice-running, it moves a ladder one rung like any other answer, and it pushes the moods below.

sound_contract.note: This file never names a sound. When a behaviour or a reaction rung starts, the engine fires a cue named below; data/sounds.json decides whether anything plays. A beat marked cue:true is the one place in it a sound may land; with no mark, the start.

names.ladder_position: also <reaction key>.<rung number> for ladders (poked.1 to poked.5)

with_every_cue: voice_spent (has a voice sound already played in this bit)

private.note: How the private behaviours (needs.watched false, tag private) come in. They unlock when the witness rule says you have gone, at ramp_start weight, and rise to full weight over ramp_s (the comedian: for the first 15 min alone, almost nothing changes). So a short absence shows one small private thing at most; a long one shows him.

moves_wanted.note: Moves this file calls that are not yet in data/moves.json. For the animator: add, rename, or tell me which existing move to call.

idles.see: One slow blink, straight at you. Nothing else moves.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: His eyes go to the cursor, stay, and come back. His body never moves.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: His eyes drift to an empty bit of desktop and stay there a second too long. Then back.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: He turns three quarters away from you and stays. His eyes are the last thing to leave.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: One deeper breath. He sags a hair and comes back up.
idles.often: direction.json breath.sigh_every_s: every 40 to 120 s

idles.see: He sinks a few percent, gets a little wider, like someone getting comfortable in a chair.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: He tracks the cursor with his eyes, then decides it is not worth it and stops while it is still moving.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: He waddles a short way, stops, and half turns back to where he was. Never edge to edge.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: He walks back to the exact spot he was standing on before, turns to his usual angle, and is satisfied.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 6 min while in this mood

idles.see: Eyes locked on the cursor, a slow lean toward it. If it comes his way he looks off a beat too fast.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: He walks to the edge of the screen and leans out past it like looking round a corner. Comes back with nothing to report.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 8 min while in this mood

idles.see: He leans toward wherever the cursor last stopped and narrows his eyes at it.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 3 min while in this mood

idles.see: He works out where the cursor is heading and his eyes get there first. When it arrives he is already looking at it.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: He looks up at whatever is above him, leans back to see more, nearly goes over, catches it.
idles.often: about once every 3 to 9 min while in this mood

idles.see: He looks down at the spot under him, steps off it, and looks at the spot.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 7 min while in this mood

idles.see: A glance, back, then a sharp second look at the same thing.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: He turns all the way round to check behind him. Nothing. He turns back, slower.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 6 min while in this mood

idles.see: He ends up nearer to where you are working. By accident. He is facing the other way.
idles.often: about once every 4 to 12 min while in this mood

idles.see: The smirk comes in slowly. One slow blink. He holds it.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: One small bounce. Then he stands as if he had not done that.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 6 min while in this mood

idles.see: He looks away with the smirk on, then peeks to check you are still looking.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 3 min while in this mood

idles.see: He turns to give you his better side and holds it there.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 8 min while in this mood

idles.see: He rocks forward onto his toes once, and back. That is all.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 5 min while in this mood

idles.see: He breathes in and gets taller. Holds it. Nobody reacts. He lets it out.
idles.often: about once every 3 to 10 min while in this mood

idles.see: A slow walk across, in no hurry, looking at you the whole way.
idles.often: about once every 4 to 11 min while in this mood

idles.see: He turns his back on you completely and stays there. After a long time, a quarter turn to peek. Then away again.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 6 min while in this mood

idles.see: One foot nub taps. Uneven. It speeds up, then stops dead.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: A snap turn away from you and a stiff settle.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 3 min while in this mood

idles.see: A band of him slips sideways in purple. He shoves it back with a short hard lean and a look that says nothing happened.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: A sharp breath out: a quick drop and rise. One small sound.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 6 min while in this mood

idles.see: He waddles to the far side, fast, and stops facing away.
idles.often: about once every 3 to 9 min while in this mood

idles.see: His eyes come round to the cursor and stay there far too long. Then he lets it go.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: He goes to the edge of the screen and stands facing it, an inch away.
idles.often: about once every 5 to 15 min while in this mood

idles.see: He moves exactly one step further from the cursor, without looking at it. Just the one.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: A small shake goes through him, his eyes dart both ways, and then he freezes into being calm.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: A fast look behind him. And back.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: He holds too still. Breath shallow. One eye twitches. A long breath out.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 3 min while in this mood

idles.see: Well after it is over, one late twitch. He checks whether you saw.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: He looks at each edge of the screen in turn, as if working out which way he would go.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: Wide eyes travel slowly across the whole screen, one end to the other.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 4 min while in this mood

idles.see: A one-step glitch knocks a band of him out of line. Startled. He settles it back in and covers at once. No hop.
idles.often: about once every 4 to 12 min while in this mood

idles.see: Three fast blinks in a row, uneven, like clearing something.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: He sags. His lids come down. He catches himself and stands back up, most of the way.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: A blink that lasts over a second. That may have been a nap.
idles.often: about once every 1 to 2 min while in this mood

idles.see: A long blink with a sag in it. He comes back up slower than he went down.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 8 min while in this mood

idles.see: His lids close in steps and he starts to tip. He jerks back upright.
idles.often: about once every 2 to 5 min while in this mood

idles.see: Asleep on his feet. Long slow breath. He leans a little more with each one and starts to slide.
idles.often: only once he is actually tired (energy under 0.7: about 25 min in, sooner after throws and big bits); then at most once in 7 min

idles.see: His own glitch wakes him. He looks round quickly. He was awake the whole time.
idles.often: about once every 5 to 15 min while in this mood

idles.see: He leans his side against the edge of the screen and rests there.
idles.often: about once every 4 to 13 min while in this mood

idles.see: A very slow waddle that runs out before it gets anywhere. He stops mid-step.
idles.often: about once every 3 to 10 min while in this mood

idles.see: Alone, he practises the side-eye. Too much brow. Too little. There. From his usual angle, never turned front. He looks round after.
idles.often: about once every 5 to 15 min while in this mood

idles.see: He tries a spinning hop. It does not come off. He stands very still and looks round.
idles.often: about once every 10 to 30 min while in this mood

idles.see: He balances on one foot nub. Wobbles. Nearly goes. Saves it.
idles.often: about once every 6 to 18 min while in this mood

idles.see: He looks the way he always looks, at nothing, for a long time. Lids and brows ease. The side-eye stays: it is his face.
idles.often: about once every 4 to 12 min while in this mood

idles.see: Tipped forward 0.12 rad, eyes down, one small nod per spot, 40 frames apart. He loses count and starts again.
idles.often: about once every 7 to 21 min while in this mood

idles.see: He sets off a small glitch in himself, on purpose, and watches it go.
idles.often: about once every 8 to 24 min while in this mood

idles.see: The cursor has not moved in a while. He walks over and checks it: one small bump with his side. Nothing. He goes back to his spot.
idles.often: about once every 15 to 45 min while in this mood

idles.see: He lets himself down into a sit: lower, wider, done. He stays like that.
idles.often: about once every 8 to 25 min while in this mood

idles.see: He looks left. He looks right. Fries. He leans in face first and comes up with one sticking out of his mouth, and eats it holding your eye. Come close and he turns his back and keeps eating.
idles.often: rare on his own: at most once in 15 min; the fed reaction also plays it on demand

idles.see: He looks across the room, thinks about it, walks there and stands as if he had always stood there. One look back at where he was.
Something over there. He goes to see. It was nothing. He inspects it anyway.
He has had enough of this spot. He turns his back, walks to another one, and stands there with his back still to you for a while.
A brisk walk to somewhere else, as if he had an appointment there. A look left, a look right. He did not.
A slow waddle across the floor with a stop in the middle of it for no reason. He arrives, sags, and that is where he lives now.

poked.note: One rung up per poke. The whole ladder resets after reset_after_quiet_s of peace. The dent itself is spud.poke(point, normal, power) and happens on every rung. The steps and their frames are the comedian's (design/gags.json poke_ladder); after the bite the next ladder starts at rung 2, so he never plays the same step twice running. Round 3 (comedian): rung four keeps his back to you and takes one step away (never a second about-face); the bite is CUT (no mouth you can see at 100 px, no hang): rung five is the walk-off.

rungs.see: Only his eyes move: to the cursor, and back.
He glares at the cursor and holds it.
He turns his back on you.
A flicker, one step away, and his back is still to you. He never turns round to do it.
He walks off. You wanted to bother him; now you have a potato, over there. He does not come back for 20 seconds.

poked_asleep.note: Wins over the poke ladder while he is asleep; does not move the ladder.

variants.see: He starts awake and at once pretends he was awake.
One eye opens. It looks at you. It closes again.

picked_up.note: Physics owns his body while held (hang from the grab point, bottom swinging behind). These pick the acting. Repeats inside repeat_window_s climb escalate[].

variants.see: He hangs there with no expression at all, looking straight ahead.
He looks down at how far the ground is. Then at you.
He glares at the cursor for as long as you hold him.
He does not wake up. He hangs, asleep.
He has learned. Lids down, face set, braced for the throw before you do it.

dragged.note: Continuous while held and moving. speed = pointer speed in body heights per second; shakes = direction reversals per second.

rings.see: Carried slowly: his eyes stay on where he was standing.
Carried fast: his eyes go to where he is headed, face still flat.
Shaken or whirled: his eyes go with it for a lap and a half, then stop following, and close. He will not be made to do that. Set down, he walks off without looking back.

thrown.note: In the air the body is physics. The face stays FLAT (deadpan) until the first hard contact, where it may break to shock for at most 2 impact frames + break_hold_s. Then one aftermath, never the same as the last. hard and through are set by the engineer's thresholds (inputs.throw).

variants.see: He settles. A held beat. Then his eyes come slowly round to you.
He lands and carries on as if that was where he was going.
He looks himself over, side to side, to see that it is all still there.
He stays flat where he landed, longer than is comfortable. Then peels himself up.
He gets up and walks all the way back to the exact spot you took him from. Turns to his usual angle. Looks at you.
He hits the wall and stays there, flat. He looks at you from the wall. Then he peels off top first and falls on his face.
He lands on his feet, dead clean. For an instant he is as surprised as you. Then it was the plan. Then one foot nub slips.
Thrown too gently to bother tumbling. He lands already looking at you. That was it?
He was asleep and stays asleep through the whole arc. He wakes a second after he has landed.
No settle bounce, no look away: he stares at you from wherever he ended up.

cracked.note: A throw hard enough to crack the glass. Plays INSTEAD of a thrown aftermath. The crack is the engineer's; it comes LATE (after he settles and a held half second), at most once every 10 min, and any click clears it. Frames: design/gags.json crack. With three or more Potatoes the blame chain plays (crowd.bits).

variants.see: He looks at the crack. He looks at you. Then he walks over and stands in front of it, shuffling to stay between it and your cursor, face blank. It fades behind him. He steps aside: nothing there.
He looks at the crack. He looks at you. He leaves it to fade.

went_through.note: Thrown hard enough to go through the wallpaper into the 404: at most once every 30 min (under that, the same throw gives the crack or a wall splat). He is gone for away_s and NOTHING fills the pause. Then one return, never the same as last time. A click shuts the hole early and he walks in at once. Round 3: the nothing is 200 f (it was built at 297), he walks in ONE body height from the edge OPPOSITE the hole, looks at the hole 40 f, at you 50 f, and the hole shuts 24 f into the look at you (comedian, director). The clip is the animator's and the hole is the engineer's: these are the numbers for them; the brain adds nothing on top.

variants.see: He walks in from the opposite edge, unhurried, as if he had been somewhere. Stops. Looks at the hole. Looks at you. The hole shuts.
The same walk, but something has come back with him that he has not noticed, stuck to a foot nub or his back. He notices. Shakes it off. It blinks out.
His eyes appear in the dark of the hole, looking out at your desktop. Then at you. Then they go back in. Another pause. Then he walks in from the edge.

dropped.note: Let go slowly (below the throw threshold). The plop and its one overshoot are the rig's (moves.json set_down).

variants.see: Plop. He goes back to exactly what he was doing.
Plop. He looks up at where he was a moment ago.
Plop. He shuffles one step away from your cursor.
Plop. He has been put down facing the wrong way and takes his time turning back.

landed.note: Every landing, his own hops included. speed = impact speed in body heights per second. The squash is the rig's and the flesh kick is the animator's secondary.jiggle (not spud.land(): it rings three times). These add the acting. A thrown aftermath replaces this on the final rest of a throw.

rings.see: A soft plop and one overshoot. No acting.
A firm landing: wider squash, a blink on the way back up.
A hard one: flat for a beat, the face breaks, and it takes a moment to come back.

ignored.note: Time-driven. quiet_s = seconds since the last input aimed at him. Any direct input resets it to the bottom. Rungs do not play clips: each switches behaviours on (prefer) and pushes moods, and the picker does the rest. Nothing on it asks for attention: he never knocks, never waves, never comes to get you. Two sides: while you are there but busy (watched), and while you are gone (unwatched: the comedian's hour).

rungs.see: You are busy elsewhere. He looks at you a little more often than he would like.
He ends up nearer to where you are working. By accident. Facing the other way.
He gives up on you and does something for himself: the edge, the lean, the fries.
You have gone. For a long while nothing changes: unbothered is home.
His own business: the private behaviours come at full weight.
He drifts over and stands near the cursor. Looks at it. It does not move. Looks again, closer.
He leans on it the way you lean on a lamp post. It holds.
He is asleep, leaning on your cursor. If the cursor is not over the window he sleeps where he stands, and slides.

the_fall.see: You move the mouse. The thing he was leaning on is gone. He hangs on nothing for six frames, drops, plop. He is up at once, looking somewhere else. He was not asleep.

cursor_gone.note: THE WITNESS RULE (direction.json witness): the cursor has not moved for watched.gone_after_s. No clip: he lets the act go and the private behaviours unlock.

variants.see: A beat after you have gone, his shoulders come down, so to speak: a slow settle, and the side-eye relaxes a notch.

cursor_returned.note: The mouse moves after he thought you had gone. Snap in watched.back_snap_ms, hold the cover for watched.back_cover_hold_ms. The cover-up is always a beat too fast. Whatever private behaviour was running ends through its exit:'cover'.

variants.see: A tiny start, and he is standing exactly as he always stands, a shade too still.
A tiny start, and he is very interested in something on the other side of the screen.
He was asleep. He is not asleep. He was never asleep.

cursor_near.note: Continuous. Distances from direction.json eyes.cursor_track_*. Leaving a ring fast (cursor speed over fast_px_s) while he was looking plays caught_looking instead of a blend out.

rings.see: Eyes on it, and a lean you could deny.
The cursor is parked beside him. He sidesteps one body width without looking at it. Park it again: he sidesteps again. The third time he does not move. He looks at it, and holds, until you leave.
steps: does not move: look cursor, hold until it leaves

rings.see: It is right on his face. His eyes cross onto the tip, and he leans back from it exactly as far as it came forward.

caught_looking.see: Caught: his eyes leave a beat too fast and stay away a beat too long.

click_nearby.see: A click near him, not on him: one blink. Nothing else.

window_edge.note: He has reached an edge of the screen under his own power. (Being thrown into one is physics + thrown.)

variants.see: He stops just short of it, looks at it, and turns round.
He was watching you instead of where he was going. He walks into it. It did not happen.
He leans out past it for a look.
He leans on it.

typed_at.note: Someone is typing TO him (his own text box has focus). We never listen to typing anywhere else. chars = length so far. On send the words go to the real brain (the real one) or the script's own engine (first-batch.json); this file only covers the listening.

rings.see: He turns a little toward the words and waits.
His eyes move along the line in small steps as it grows.
It is getting long. His eyes widen a little with every extra line, then narrow.
You stopped typing without sending. He looks at the words, then at you.

other_near.note: Another Potato has come inside crowd.notice. Tracked per pair. Past the last rung the pair goes to crowd.social (clump or argue).

rungs.see: The older one turns to look. The new one turns to look. They hold it. Both turn home on the same frame, as if neither had.

pair.frames: older turns at +20 (0.51 rad, 14 f), newer at +38, both hold to +86, both units end on +86 and both turn home from there

rungs.see: They side-eye each other. The same side-eye.
One of them shuffles a little closer. Stops. Looks away.

zapped.note: Nothing is added to him (no hair, no char). The zap itself (stepped purple at 12 fps, outline to binary or wireframe for a beat, a puff) is the animator's and engineer's. This is the acting after, including the late twitch.

variants.see: Brows stuck up, eyes wide, standing taller than usual. The brows come down one at a time. Then the side-eye, at you.
He holds perfectly still and decides it did not happen. A wisp gives him away.

late_twitch.see: Two seconds after he has decided it is over: one twitch. Silent.

fed.note: Fries offered by the user. Same bit as the idle 'fries', started on demand; frames are design/gags.json fries_eye_contact, fries_caught (the cursor inside turn_back_px while a fry is in his mouth: freeze, turn away, keep chewing) and fries_empty_carton. He never offers you one.

variants.see: He looks left. He looks right. He eats one, looking right at you.
He takes them and turns his back first. All you see is the chew.

squished.note: The explode gag's wrong-version beat waits on the Potato seat's call (gags.json explode.needs_potato_seat_ok). Pressed flat and let go (squish), hit flat against something (splat), or burst (explode). All three end in him coming back together: slightly wrong first, corrected, then he checks who saw.

variants.see: He rebuilds in purple, a little wrong (too tall, or leaning). Notices. Corrects it. Looks to see who saw.
He comes back together slowly, eyes first, and the eyes are already on you.

shaken_walk_off.note: Played after being shaken, once he is on the ground.

variants.see: He opens his eyes, and walks away from the cursor without looking at it.

reaction_rules.never_twice_running: mode variants: never the variant played last time for this event (if only one is eligible, it plays with its sides flipped and ranges redrawn). mode ladder: the rung always moves. mode rings: continuous, chosen by the measured value.
reaction_rules.choose_variant: Among eligible variants (when true, not the last one): weight by moods affinity if the variant has one, else equal. If the event is inside its repeat_window_s, take the next entry of escalate instead.
reaction_rules.push: Applied when the rung or variant starts. push_per_s:true = applied every second while the ring is active.
reaction_rules.after_any_reaction: He does not go straight back to an idle: hold for one gap of the (new) dominant mood, then pick. The interrupted behaviour only resumes if the rung says resume.

look_after.rule: Round 3 (comedian: the look after is the joke and it ran on the brain's clock; director B4: it has to be a turn). In every aftermath of mine the look at you starts no later than 36 frames after he is standing, is a turn of the body (0.36 rad) with the eyes, and holds 48 to 57 frames before anything else in the row. Nothing else of the brain's can start on him while a reaction runs. When the throw ended in the animator's own crack / hole / splat clip, her clip has the look in it: the brain plays NO second aftermath (that was the walk that cut the crack look at frame 401) and holds him after_her_clip_f frames.

crowd.note: Up to five in one scene. One is on the real brain, the rest run this file alone, each bent by a personality. A kitchen at 2 am, not a chorus line.

who_is_who.real: One Potato, tan, may take words from the real brain. For movement it runs this same file like the others; the brain may only ASK for a behaviour by id (request), and the ask goes through the same picker rules and the same stage.
who_is_who.script: Up to four. Each is given one personality id from game/personalities/first-batch.json, no two the same.

notice.first_time_fires: other_near for both, the second one stagger_ms later
notice.again_note: A pair standing in notice range climbs the other_near ladder one rung each time this clock fires, once. It only starts over if they part and meet again (so it can never become a loop).
notice.settle_note: Round 3 (director B3): nobody notices a newcomer until he has landed and stood for settle_s. It used to fire at 0.3 s, while he was still dropping in.

space.rule: Inside personal space with no bit running: the one with less fed_up yields a step (door-holder always yields).

clumps.shape: 2 + 2 + 1 (with five; 2 + 1 with three; 2 + 2 with four has no odd one, so one of a pair wanders off every so often)
clumps.who_goes_odd: Never the same Potato twice running. The odd one is chosen from the pair that has stood together longest: the one with the higher fed_up or low_power walks off; the old odd one drifts to the gap.

facing.note: Potato seat: in a clump no two face the same way, so each side-eye lands on someone. Radians of yaw; in a pair the left one is turned 0.5 toward his partner and the right one 0.3 toward his; the odd one is turned 0.7 toward the nearest clump. This is his stance while he is in the crowd.

clumps.built_note: Round 3: built (crowd.tonight.clumps). Every odd_one_changes_every_s (45 to 110 s here, so three minutes shows it change) the room is re-dealt: the odd one is never the one it was last time; of the rest the most fed up or lowest on power walks off; the groups take drawn places along the floor. The sleeper is never moved. Not while an argument or a pile-up runs.

stage.rule: ONE BIG BIT AT A TIME. A single stage token for the whole scene. A big behaviour, an argument from rung 3 up, and any user throw take it. While it is held, nobody else may start a big behaviour: they are the audience.
stage.bid: A Potato wanting the stage bids its picker score x (1 + showman dial). Highest bid wins; ties go to whoever held it longest ago.
stage.user_always_wins: Anything the user does to any Potato takes the stage at once.

audience.stagger_ms: direction.json crowd.reaction_stagger_ms, a fresh draw per Potato, in order of distance from the bit

reactions.see: Eyes follow the bit. Body stays put.
A side-eye at whoever is doing it.
Leans out to see past another Potato.
A Potato is picked up or thrown: every head follows it across, a beat apart.
Reacts a full second after everyone else.

audience.rule: No two neighbours choose the same audience reaction. At most one aud_late per bit. After the bit: each looks at the cursor or at each other, staggered, never all at once.

bits.note: Round 3: a bit listed here gets only these reactions from everyone awake in range (still staggered by distance). A Potato picked up or thrown, by you or by another Potato: every body turns after him and turns again when he crosses them; then each looks at you.

in_sync_gag.see: All of them look at the cursor on the same frame. Hold. Then back to it, one by one.

bits.note: The comedian's crowd gags (design/gags.json owns frames, cool-downs and chances). Each needs the stage. This file says when they may be bid for.

shove_chain.when: an argument reaches rung 4 with a third Potato within 1.5 body widths behind the one shoved

pile_up.when: a thrown Potato comes to rest within one body width of two others
pile_up.tonight: three or more at rest inside one body width of the next after a shove or a throw
pile_up.within_note: bodies keep about one body width apart on contact, so one exactly would never fire

not_listening.when: an argument is running and a Potato is asleep inside notice range of it (the sleeper's personality first)

crack_blame_chain.when: cracked with three or more Potatoes: replaces the single crack aftermath

take_one_away.when: the user picks one up mid-argument: the rest play aud_tennis, his opponent bursts once more at the empty spot, and when he is set down the ladder is one rung lower

the_real_one_is_late.rule: The tan one runs on the real brain, so in an argument he is always a beat behind: while the brain is busy he plays the gather hold; when the answer lands he delivers his burst to whoever is nearest, even if they have turned away. With no brain connected he runs this file like the rest and a fixed late_s stands in.

cast.rule: Never the same five twice running. Which four scripts stand with the tan one is drawn at launch, never the last launch's draw; the comedian's first cast and bench are in design/gags.json crowd_cast.

arguments.note: How two of them get into it, how it climbs to a shove, and how it ends. Slapstick between equals: REAL, NOT MEAN.

who_starts.score: fed_up weight x 1.0 + nosy weight x 0.4 + boredom x 0.5 + personality instigate - 0.6 if he started the last one - 1.0 if he won the last one
who_starts.needs: score over 0.55, no argument in the last gap_s, both awake, neither held by the user
who_starts.crowded_note: standing inside another's personal space pushes fed_up a little every second: it is why five in a kitchen end up arguing

arguments.who_with: The nearest Potato in his facing cone that he did not argue with last time and that was not thrown in the last protect_s. Never the same pair twice running.

ladder.see: A look that lasts too long. The other looks back.
One leans in. The other leans in. Nobody blinks.
ladder.round3_note: Comedian: (1) bob 7 to 9% of his height with a 0.08 rad tip toward the other on each down, 8 f a bob, 3 to 5 a burst (it was 3 to 4.5%: 2 to 4 pixels). The animator's beat() caps a bob at 5% and has no tip yet: hers to raise. (2) the speaker keeps his turn toward the other until he is answered (the unit keeps its yaw). (3) a script reply skips the gather and is timed off the speaker's bob beat, so its bobs start overlap_s (6 to 10 f) before his end. The tan one keeps his whole gather and his late_s: three overlapping and one thinking.

ladder.see: A bump with the side of the body. A bump back. Each sends a real dent and a wobble through the other.
A proper shove: gather, drive, the other skids a body width and settles. Then it is the other one's turn. Twenty frames after it lands the shover looks away and up, for 48.

One gets under the other to throw him. Gather. Heave. The other rises two pixels. A long strain. Down. One time in four it works, and then it is the same throw the user does: same physics, same aftermaths.

burst.what: The unit of every argument from rung 2 up: a lean in plus 2 to 4 short body bobs, 0.4 to 0.67 s. The reply starts 0.1 to 0.17 s BEFORE the other has finished: the overlap is what makes it an argument. Each exchange is 15% bigger and 0.1 body widths closer. Four exchanges at most, then the rung is rolled. Round 3: bobs are 7 to 9% with a tip, 3 to 5 a burst; replies overlap by 6 to 10 f measured from the bob itself.
burst.about: Always something you can see: the last fry, one spot they both want to stand on, whose fault the crack is. The engine picks the nearest of those that exists; with none, the spot one of them is standing on.

arguments.climb_chance: the rung's climb x (0.6 + the pair's mean fed_up weight) x personality patience. Roll once at the end of each rung from the instigator's stream. Fail = it ends here by backing down.
arguments.turns: From rung 3 the two alternate: whoever just took one gives the next one. Nobody lands two in a row.
arguments.who_wins: The winner of the top rung reached is rolled 50/50, then: the winner of the previous argument cannot win this one (nobody wins twice in a row), the instigator's chance drops to 0.4 (starting it does not pay), and the tan one gets no edge: he loses as often as anyone.

ends.see: One breaks the look first and finds something else to look at. The other gets a little smug.
They stand with their backs to each other. After a while one peeks. If the other is peeking too, both snap away.
ends.who_peeks: the loser peeks first; never the same peeker as last time

ends.see: The user does something. Both stop mid-bit and look at the cursor, staggered. It is forgotten.
A third Potato walks straight between them without looking at either. The moment is gone.

after.make_up: 40 to 120 s later the pair may play other_near rung 3 (one shuffles closer, looks away). That is the whole apology.

not_mean: The comedian's slapstick line (design/gags.json slapstick_line) is law: nobody is the target twice running; nobody is hit while down or asleep on purpose; every loser gets the next look at the audience; the tan one loses as often as anyone.
Two at a time. Nobody joins in against one; the rest are audience.
Never start on a Potato who is asleep, low on energy (under 0.3), mid-rebuild, or in the user's hand.
A Potato thrown by anyone (user or Potato) cannot be argued with for protect_s.
At most one throw between Potatoes every throw_gap_s.
The loser always gets the last look: his aftermath plays in full, on the stage, before anything else starts.
Nobody wins twice in a row; nobody is picked on twice in a row.
The face stays flat through the whole fight. No angry face over k 0.6, no gloating beyond a smirk_hold.
A personality's 'wont' always beats the ladder (personalities.wont).

shoved_after.see: He settles where the shove left him, and looks at who did it.

take_one_away.see: You took one of them out of it. The other bursts once more at the empty spot.

owed_burst.see: UNFINISHED BUSINESS: long after you broke it up, he walks over and delivers the one burst he was owed. To a back, if that is what is there. Then he leaves.

referee.see: One of the others, the nearest standing, looks at the one on the floor, then at the one who did it, and rules nothing.

heat.note: Round 3 (director B3: in any three minutes of five, one argument climbs to a shove; comedian: a shove inside the first 90 s, most runs; once a session one gets thrown). The room OWES a shove: when shove_due_s has passed with none, the next argument (which starts sooner: gap_when_due_s) climbs rung by rung to the shove without rolling. After a shove the clock is shove_due_later_s. Every guard still stands (never the same giver on the same taker twice running, never one who is down or asleep, a wont beats the ladder). Once a session, after throw_once_after_s, a rung-4 argument climbs once more and the lift WORKS: an impulse up and over, capped at the script-throw speed, then the same flight, landing and aftermath as a throw by you. off: on = false (the ladder rolls every rung again, as in the Build round).

reactions.freeze_then_look: Everyone awake stops dead for a beat, then looks at whoever is mid-step.
reactions.look_at_self: Each looks down at himself, one after another. The tan one last.
reactions.step_onto_spot: The nearest one walks onto the exact spot he means and stands on it.
reactions.look_away_whistle: Everyone looks somewhere else at once, a beat apart.
reactions.argue_back: The one most ready for a fight turns and starts an argument with him at rung 2.
reactions.look_at_him_long: A long look at him from everyone. Nobody says anything.
reactions.look_at_sleeper: They all look at the one asleep. He does not wake.
reactions.look_at_last_shover: They look at whoever shoved last. He looks at the floor.
reactions.keep_going: The one who keeps going keeps going: a burst straight over him.
reactions.matching_side_eye: The nearest one gives him his own side-eye back.
reactions.all_look_cursor: They look at the cursor. Then pointedly do not.
reactions.back_down: If an argument is running it ends there: both back down.

thinking_one.not_listening: A Potato who is asleep, or whose dial is hurry, never reacts to a line. That is the one who isn't listening.

personalities.note: How a script Potato's entry in game/personalities/first-batch.json BENDS this file. Nothing is forked: same idles, same reactions, same ladders. Five fields of the entry are read, nothing else.

reads.change.dial + change.move: Looks up dials below; every number in the dial is scaled by move / 2.

reads.tell.glitch_kind: Replaces 'kind' in every glitch beat he plays.
reads.tell.pet_word: May appear as small faint glitch text (Major Mono Display) inside his own glitch, at most once every 3 minutes. Never a label, never a speech bubble.
reads.glitch_colour: His glitch colour and body tint, as the director set (the real one is tan and purple).
reads.wont: Read by a person, written here as hard rules under wont. A wont always wins.

wont_rules.note: The wont lines above as rules the engine can run. A wont always wins.

overnight.note: BOLD CHOICE (Behaviour Designer). He remembers how you left it. When the host shuts him down it saves the small state below; on the next launch the state comes back, faded by how long he was off, and bends his first minutes. Throw him at the wall last night and he starts today with his back to you. He never greets you either way. Off with flags.overnight.value = false.

fade.rule: Each saved mood pressure keeps 0.5^(hours_off / half_life_hours) of its distance from rest. Energy restores at the asleep rate for the hours off.

cap.rule: It can colour his first minute, never lock him in a mood. After max_opening_s the normal picker runs with nothing forced. Potato seat: 12 s, not 40; the back must peek inside it (the peek makes it a grudge, not a sulk); first launch ever carries nothing.

openings.see: He is already standing with his back to you.
He is already looking at the edges of the screen, one after another.
He is where you left him, with the smirk still on.
You were gone for days. He is asleep against the edge of the screen and does not wake for you.
Nothing carried. He is just there.

overnight.determinism: The carried state is an INPUT to the run and is written in the trace header. Strips and tests pass an empty state.
overnight.in_the_game: The game passes its own save (or nothing). The desktop keeps one small local file. Nothing personal is stored: six numbers, three counters and a time.
